item.title: NSL sponsorship questioned
item.description: The Nambawan Super Limited three-year sponsorship, of the PNG Chief’s Rugby League Club, has been questioned by the TISA Group. TISA Group Chief Executive Officer, Michael Koisen in a statement says, the TISA Group, wants to know, what the value of the sponsorship is, and what value it will be bringing back to its members.
item.content:encoded:
The Nambawan Super Limited three-year sponsorship, of the PNG Chief’s Rugby League Club, has been questioned by the TISA Group.

TISA Group Chief Executive Officer, Michael Koisen in a statement says, the TISA Group, wants to know, what the value of the sponsorship is, and what value it will be bringing back to its members.

Koisen says that the primary purpose of a superannuation fund is to protect, grow and safeguard the retirement savings of its members, and he is not sure, if such a high-profile sports sponsorship, should be a priority to use member funds.

He says that the issue is not whether rugby league is popular, but they are concern if such expenditure delivers a measurable benefit to its members.

Mr. Koisen also says that the members have a right to know how much of their money has been committed, what financial return is expected from the sponsorship, how it will be measured, and will the sponsorship improve retirement outcomes for its members.

He further adds that those funds would have been better directed toward member services, fee reductions, digital improvements, financial literacy initiatives, or enhancing long-term investment performance.

Mr. Koisen further adds that while sponsorships may generate publicity and brand exposure, publicity alone is not a member benefit, and the critical question is whether the expenditure creates value that can be objectively demonstrated and justified.

item.title: PNG Fire Service deploys firefighters to combat Manus bushfire
item.description: ​The PNG Fire Service has deployed a team of twenty firefighters today from Port Moresby to Lou Island, Manus Province, to assist local communities in responding to an escalating bushfire that threatens homes, local infrastructure, and vital food gardens. Chief of Fire Services Bill Roo says the ongoing blaze poses a significant risk to the livelihoods and food security of the island’s residents.
item.content:encoded:
​The PNG Fire Service has deployed a team of twenty firefighters today from Port Moresby to Lou Island, Manus Province, to assist local communities in responding to an escalating bushfire that threatens homes, local infrastructure, and vital food gardens.

Chief of Fire Services Bill Roo says the ongoing blaze poses a significant risk to the livelihoods and food security of the island’s residents.

He said despite facing operational challenges and a shortage of specialised bushfire equipment, the deployed personnel remain fully committed to working directly with local residents to protect lives, property, and community assets.

Chief Roo outlined that the response team will prioritize community collaboration, risk mitigation, and containment strategy through five key operational pillars:

1. ​Firebreak Operations: Partnering with local residents to establish strategic firebreaks aimed at halting the fire's spread toward homes and crop gardens.

2. ​Community Fire Safety Awareness: Conducting on-the-ground educational sessions on bushfire prevention, safety protocols, and emergency readiness.

3. ​Community Coordination: Working alongside traditional leaders and local authorities to coordinate unified mitigation efforts.

4. ​Situation Reporting: Monitoring ground conditions and reporting on operational challenges to identify needed resources for ongoing response and recovery.

​"Due to limited specialized equipment, our team’s primary operational focus centers on community partnership and containment," said Chief of Fire Services. "All activities will be carried out with the highest priority placed on the safety of both our firefighters and the local community."

​The PNG Fire Service expressed gratitude to Acting Director of the National Disaster Centre (NDC), Laso Mana, for his leadership and support in facilitating the rapid deployment of officers to Manus Province.

​"This deployment highlights the vital importance of inter-agency cooperation and strong leadership in serving Papua New Guinea," Chief Roo added. "Working together across government bodies allows us to respond effectively to disasters and safeguard our people during critical times. Fire safety remains a shared responsibility."

item.title: PNG Chiefs launch historic logo and supporter jersey ahead of 2028 NRL entry
item.description: The PNG Chiefs have marked a watershed moment ahead of their entry into the NRL Telstra Premiership in 2028, officially unveiling their inaugural logo and supporter jersey in Port Moresby today. The launch event was held at Santos Stadium in Boroko, attended by representatives from the Papua New Guinea and Australian Governments, the PNG Chiefs and the NRL.
item.content:encoded:
The PNG Chiefs have marked a watershed moment ahead of their entry into the NRL Telstra Premiership in 2028, officially unveiling their inaugural logo and supporter jersey in Port Moresby today.

The launch event was held at Santos Stadium in Boroko, attended by representatives from the Papua New Guinea and Australian Governments, the PNG Chiefs and the NRL.

The logo was designed by a team of Papua New Guinean graphic artists, while the jersey features cultural drawings by renowned local artist TABU.

As the NRL's newest club representing the world's most linguistically diverse nation with more than 800 languages, the PNG Chiefs say the logo represents more than just a city or province - it represents all of Papua New Guinea.

The mark is a chief formed from elements drawn from across PNG: from the Highlands to the Islands, from Momase to the Southern coastline.

The chief was chosen as the central figure because across PNG's many cultures, he represents leadership, earned authority and custodianship of his people.

The logo is comprised of four key elements:

PNG Chiefs CEO Lorna McPherson said today is one of the most significant milestones for the club.

"Today marks one of the most significant milestones in the journey of the PNG Chiefs. This is the first time that our club has its true, complete identity – a logo and jersey that our players, partners and fans can hold to as their own.

"The jersey is more than what players wear when they take to the field – it is a symbol of belonging, unity and the opportunity to represent millions of Papua New Guineans on the national stage," she said.

"There will only ever be one logo and one first jersey, and today we take a huge step forward in truly bringing the PNG Chiefs to life."

PNG Chiefs Chair Catherine Harris said the identity belongs to the people of PNG.

"I am proud to celebrate our logo and jersey, which are unmistakeably Papua New Guinean. In reflecting the culture, character and pride of the nation, this identity belongs to more than the club – it belongs to the people of Papua New Guinea."

Kumuls stars and 2028 PNG Chiefs Development players Gairo Voro, Morea Morea and Finley Glare modelled the new supporter jersey at the launch.

The supporter kit features the club's foundation corporate partners including Principal Partner BSP, PNG LNG, Coca-Cola, Nambawan Super, SP Lager, Struddys, Taylor Pacific, Toyota t/a as Ela Motors and K92 Mining.

Fans in PNG will be able to purchase the official supporter jersey from licensed outlets throughout the country, while fans in Australia and beyond can order online.

item.title: Kumuls names to face star-studded Toa Samoa
item.description: The PNG Kumuls line up for their second Rugby League World Cup fixture against Toa Samoa was named today with minor changes. London Broncos prop Epel Kapinias has been promoted to the first thirteen with Valentine Richard moved to the bench.
item.content:encoded:
The PNG Kumuls line up for their second Rugby League World Cup fixture against Toa Samoa was named today with minor changes.

London Broncos prop Epel Kapinias has been promoted to the first thirteen with Valentine Richard moved to the bench.

Another notable change is Manly's Josh Feledy named as an interchange, likely to make his debut this Saturday.

The rest of the team remains the similar with the back five, Morea Morea, Dudley Dotoi, Zac Laybutt, Nene Macdonald and Robert Derby.

The halves, Gairo Voro and Bailey Biondi Odo with Finley Glare on the bench.

Luca Moretti pairs with Kapinias up front, Edwin Ipape is the hooker and the back row features skipper Rhyse Martin, Nixon Putt and Jack De Belin at lock.

Roderick Tai, Khaiya Waeimbi and Liam Horne have been named as the other Interchange players.

The reserves; Sylvester Namo, Sanny Wabo and Zev John.

After their 42-18 victory over Lebanon, PNG Kumuls Coach Jason Demetriou called on fans to turn up in numbers and support them against a star-studded Samoan outfit.

"We will need all the support we can get,' he said.

Toa Samoa are scheduled to touch down in Port Moresby tomorrow and have named a similar side with minor changes.

Dean Mariner who sustained a hamstring in their 78-4 win over France is out with Storm flyer Sua Fa'alogo named to start at wing.

The big names in the likes skipper and incoming PNG Chiefs Jarome Luai and Brian To'o are also named along with Hamiso Tabuai Fidow at fullback, Stephan Crighton at centre and Junior Paulo as prop.

Coach Ben Gardiner said they are looking forward to running out in Port Moresby this Saturday.

"We know some of our players are loved over there," he said.

"The Samoan community in PNG have reached out and they will be backing us."

item.title: MRDC acquires Mobil service stations
item.description: The Mineral Resources Development Company [MRDC]will take over Exxon Mobil's Mobil Oil New Guinea Ltd retail fuel business. This follows the signing of the retail fuel partnership in Port Moresby on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Mineral Resources Development Company [MRDC]will take over Exxon Mobil's Mobil Oil New Guinea Ltd retail fuel business.

This follows the signing of the retail fuel partnership in Port Moresby on Tuesday.

Exxon Mobil Chairman and Managing Director Dinesh Sivasamboo says this transaction will help them focus more on bringing in fuel supplies to the country.

The acquisition will be undertaken by Star Mountain Service Station Limited [SMSSL], an investment company owned by three MRDC.

MRDC Managing Director Augustine Mano said the acquisition forms part of MRDC’s strategy to strengthen and diversify its investment portfolio in the downstream energy sector.

item.title: KPHL declares K400 million dividend
item.description: As the country continues to face economic challenges, including the impacts of El Niño, Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited has delivered some positive news. Today, Chairman of the national oil and gas company, Isaac Lupari, announced K400 million as interim dividend to the Government for this year.
item.content:encoded:
As the country continues to face economic challenges, including the impacts of El Niño, Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited has delivered some positive news.

Today, Chairman of the national oil and gas company, Isaac Lupari, announced K400 million as interim dividend to the Government for this year.

Lupari noted that between 2014 and 2025, KPHL paid K1.8 billion in taxes and K3.4 billion in dividends to the State from the PNG LNG project.

In total, the company has paid almost K5 billion to the State.

Upon receiving the cheque, Prime Minister James Marape, commended the KPHL board and management for their performance.

Marape says the dividend reflects the company’s contribution to national revenue and its commitment to prudent financial management.

item.title: PNG recruitment into Australian Defence Force to be discussed
item.description: Australia’s Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles says the recruitment of Papua New Guineans into the Australian Defence Force [ADF] will be a key agenda item at the 32nd PNG–Australia Ministerial Forum in Port Moresby today. Mr Marles said discussions would focus on recruitment pathways and processes under the Pukpuk Treaty.
item.content:encoded:
Australia’s Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles says the recruitment of Papua New Guineans into the Australian Defence Force [ADF] will be a key agenda item at the 32nd PNG–Australia Ministerial Forum in Port Moresby today.

Mr Marles said discussions would focus on recruitment pathways and processes under the Pukpuk Treaty.

He said the program would be based on transparency and merit, while acknowledging PNG’s handling of its recent PNG Defence Force [PNGDF] recruitment issues.

“In respect to the PNGDF recruitment saga, that is an incident worked through by the PNG government and we very much respect that process. In terms of recruitment into the ADF, it will very much be a process which is transparent, which is merit- based and we are really excited of what this will mean in terms of having young Papua New Guineans serving in the ADF,” Mr Marles said.

He said the initiative would strengthen defence ties between the two countries while creating employment and skills development opportunities for Papua New Guineans.

“We see this as a really important opportunity for both countries. From Australia’s perspective, it builds the numbers within the ADF, and for Papua New Guineans it offers not only employment but fantastic skills and capability. Most importantly, as allies, there’s nothing more profound than wearing one nation’s uniform,” he said.

Mr Marles said further details on the recruitment process would be discussed at the forum.

item.title: Universities set own K150 entrance test fee amid high student failure rates
item.description: The government admits there is a high failure rate of uni students after the first semester every year, as universities start implementing their own criteria for admission. Higher Education Minister Kinoka Feo says individual universities in Papua New Guinea are responsible for setting the K150 test fee for Grade 12 students seeking admission, not the Department of Higher Education.
item.content:encoded:
The government admits there is a high failure rate of uni students after the first semester every year, as universities start implementing their own criteria for admission.

Higher Education Minister Kinoka Feo says individual universities in Papua New Guinea are responsible for setting the K150 test fee for Grade 12 students seeking admission, not the Department of Higher Education.

Last week, thousands of grade 12 students sat their national exams, and this week they're sitting their Special Tertiary Admissions Test -PNG [STAT-P]

STAT‑P is a tertiary admissions aptitude test used by certain national universities to assess verbal and quantitative reasoning for Grade 12 school leavers and eligible non‑school leavers.

Member for Mul Baiyer Jacob Maki raised concerns in parliament during question time today [Tuesday] about the additional test and its cost, particularly for parents from rural areas.

“At the beginning of the year, plenty are accepted, and then after the first semester or first year, there are huge dropouts, so plenty of failures. So, colleges and mostly universities are thinking, are we really getting students who have the papers we are getting, or forged papers? "Minister Feo said.

He said the test was intended to confirm that students had the qualifications stated on their Grade 12 certificates.

“That test is independent, again, I want to make it clear, it's not endorsed or supported by higher education, it's done individually by each university.”

The minister said universities operated under their own laws and had the authority to introduce such requirements.

“Of course, they operate under their own act, and so they have the authority to go ahead and set similar things. So, it's not a lot of money, it's only 150 kina.”

He defended the fee, saying it was intended to establish whether students were qualified to enter university.

The minister also pointed to government assistance for students, saying about K130 million to K140 million was spent annually to help with school fees, while K53 million had been paid this year under the higher education loan program.

He said Cabinet had approved a reversal of the existing 70-30 per cent funding arrangement, under which parents paid 70 per cent and the Government paid 30 per cent.

“30% is paid by the government and 70% by parents. And the cabinet has already given approval to reverse it. So government will now pay 70% and parents will pay 30%.”

The minister said the Government would continue supporting students to make higher education accessible to young people across the country.

He added that assistance would also be available to students whose families could not afford the remaining 30 per cent.

“So making higher education accessible to every kid in Papua New Guinea.”

Grade 12 students nationwide will end the 2026 academic year after the Stat-P test this week.
